summary: F1 from round 1 is fully resolved — both error-path tests are present, well-structured, and lock down the exact data envelope contract. F2 (recall_owner_isolation 401 assertion comment) and F3 (stale oauth/mod.rs comment) remain unaddressed, but F2 is being downgraded to optional given that Task 4's spec explicitly owns the AC13 recall change and will see the conflict in CI. F3 was already optional. No new findings. Task 2 test coverage is sufficient for merge.

round1_findings_resolution.detail: Both tests present in discovery_anonymous.rs: `prompts_get_unknown_name_returns_invalid_params` (lines 345-379) and `resources_read_bad_uri_scheme_returns_invalid_params` (lines 386-414). Each asserts HTTP 200 envelope, error code -32602, typed data.field, and data.received echoing the raw input. The tests use unwrap_or_else with panic messages rather than bare unwrap — consistent with the existing test quality in the file. The comments correctly attribute the addition to the round-1 finding.

recall_owner_isolation.rs:230 still asserts anonymous recall returns 401 with no NOTE comment. Downgrading from required because: (a) Task 4's tech-spec explicitly owns AC13 recall changes and the coder will see a failing test in CI immediately when the handler changes — the conflict is not silent, just undocumented; (b) adding a comment to recall_owner_isolation.rs is strictly a Task 4 responsibility since Task 4 is the one changing the contract. Not blocking merge of Task 2.

oauth/mod.rs:2610 still says 'initialize / tools/list are the only allowlisted JSON-RPC methods'. Still stale. No new unit tests in the oauth module for prompts/get, resources/list, resources/read allowlist behavior. The integration-level coverage in discovery_anonymous.rs is sufficient for correctness. Acceptable for merge.

passing.title: F1 error-path tests assert full typed envelope (code + data.field + data.received)
passing.detail: Both new tests go beyond checking error.code == -32602 — they also assert data.field and data.received match the exact values the production path returns. This is the correct level of precision; a refactor that swaps to a different error code or drops data.field would be caught.

passing.title: New tests correctly assert HTTP 200 for JSON-RPC errors on streamable-HTTP
passing.detail: prompts_get test includes the comment 'JSON-RPC errors travel inside a 200 envelope on streamable-HTTP; only transport-level failures bump the HTTP status' — correct and documents the non-obvious behavior. resources_read test does the same implicitly.

passing.title: enriched_tools() OnceLock change is behaviorally transparent to tests
passing.detail: Caching tools via OnceLock is a performance change only. All existing assertions still hold. No test needed for the caching mechanism itself.

passing.title: All eight tests in discovery_anonymous.rs pass; full workspace green
passing.detail: Confirmed by coder: 8/8 pass, cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast green, clippy + fmt clean.

overall_assessment: Task 2 test coverage is complete. All six TDD anchors from tasks/2.md are implemented. Both edge-case error paths from tasks/2.md §Edge cases are now covered. The two remaining round-1 items (F2, F3) are acceptable for merge — F2 is a Task 4 responsibility and F3 is cosmetic. PASS.
